new_value: coap_location_beacon host test now builds and runs on native_sim/native/64. Root cause: coap_location.c calls four OSCORE functions (coap_oscore_send_protected, coap_oscore_authorize_mutating, coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request, coap_oscore_respond_resource) but the test's stub set only covered the latter two — send_protected and authorize_mutating had no stubs, causing the link failures. Fixes: (1) src/main.c adds coap_oscore_send_protected stub (always 0 = success) and coap_oscore_authorize_mutating stub (always -ENOTSUP = unauthorized, outputs zero-initialized) matching the real coap_oscore.h signatures exactly; (2) Kconfig/prj.conf left as-is — the build now configures cleanly (the RING_BUFFER trace in the original report does not reproduce; routing_dispatch and this test both configure on the current shared workspace). Verification: native_sim/native/64 build green, ztest run 29/29 PASS (0 failures) with sanitizers per the extra_conf_files chain landed for the sibling tests, two consecutive runs stable. Codereview delegated to kimi-k3 (consolidated): stub signatures verified against coap_oscore.h (addr non-const fix), zero-init outputs before -ENOTSUP return verified, test isolation confirmed (stateless stubs, no globals). Note: the test's prj.conf sets CONFIG_TEST_RANDOM_GENERATOR=y which the original report flagged as unresolvable — it resolves on the current shared workspace (TEST_RANDOM_GENERATOR was likely the RING_BUFFER-confusion symptom, now moot). Residual: prj.conf keeps CONFIG_SLIP=n and LICHEN_COAP=n deliberately (the test stubs OSCORE itself); if a future change needs real SLIP/OSCORE in this test, the stubs must be dropped first.
